newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - March 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - March 21.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on March 21:

WASHINGTON - The smallest of the nation's major tobacco companies settled 22 state lawsuits by admitting that smoking causes cancer and other diseases, that nicotine is addictive and that the industry targets underage smokers.

WASHINGTON - In a sharp rebuke to Speaker Newt Gingrich and the Republican leadership, the House rejected a resolution that would have provided millions of dollars for investigation of campaign fund-raising abuses.
WASHINGTON - Scientists have identified a biological process that plays a key role in turning healthy cells cancerous.
WASHINGTON - The region's celebrated baby boomlet -- which also delivered nanny shortages, crowded schools and crayons on the table in chic restaurants -- is cooling down.
WASHINGTON - The truck driver charged in last week's crash that killed two people and injured seven on the Capital Beltway also faces a vehicular homicide charge in Ohio.

ABERDEEN PROVING GROUND, Md. - The highest-ranking soldier accused in the Army sex scandal was cleared of the most serious sexual abuse charges he faced and was ordered to serve four months in prison for having consensual sex with a private under his command.

KINSHASA, Zaire - Although Zaire is at war and neighboring Angola is struggling to preserve peace, close relatives and aides of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko have been smuggling hundreds of tons of weapons to farmer rebels in Angola for huge profits.
